title: Establish architecture lock, change-request, and verification controls
objective: Establish repository-backed controls that preserve the frozen architecture while enabling deliberate evolution through explicit Architecture Change Requests, stronger protected-path enforcement, revision-bound verification, and auditable governance reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical ACR identifier, template and lifecycle are repository-backed and reproducible.
Protected architecture changes are routed through an explicit ACR path and cannot be silently introduced through implementation PRs.
Architect review and Product Owner approval responsibilities are explicit and machine-checkable where applicable.
Verification evidence remains revision-bound and later material implementation changes can invalidate prior verification.
A sanctioned reconciliation mechanism exists for already-merged historical governance defects without rewriting Git history or weakening normal transition validation.
At least one auditable example demonstrates architecture-change routing and one demonstrates historical governance reconciliation.
Existing normal lifecycle transitions and evidence requirements remain enforced for ordinary work items.
non_goals: No change to CAD/BIM product-domain behavior.
No automatic approval of ACRs or work items.
No weakening of evidence requirements or transition ownership.
No rewriting of historical Git merge commits or recorded event timestamps.
No architecture-version change as part of this work item unless an explicitly approved ACR authorizes it.
risk_assumptions: ARCH-WF-001 is VERIFIED and provides the baseline state machine, schema and validator controls.
The active repository architecture is v1.1 while this governance control work item preserves the original ARCH-WF-002 issue contract targeting the v1.0 workflow-control baseline.
The reconciliation mechanism must be additive and must not create an unrestricted alternate route to VERIFIED.
All changes to protected governance definitions remain subject to Architect review and the repository's protected-path mechanism.
evidence_requirements: Deterministic governance tests for ACR routing, protected-path enforcement, revision-bound verification and historical reconciliation.
Governance validation over the complete work-item registry with exit 0.
CI evidence showing governance and protected-path checks execute on pull requests.
A reproducible example covering architecture-change approval and one covering a historical merged-record reconciliation.
Evidence that existing normal lifecycle and VERIFIED gating behavior remains unchanged.

Architect ruling on PR #101 (delivered through the session channel; GitHub cannot carry a formal REQUEST_CHANGES review because the repository owner authored the PR): CHANGES REQUESTED — not approved for merge. The implementation substance is strong (deterministic ACR lifecycle tests, revision-bound verification, staged historical reconciliation, fail-closed ACR routing, the documented and validated citation-parser fix, the three P011 failures explicitly preserved), but a blocking architectural/governance defect was found: circular ACR authorization. The protected-path model protects existing records under governance/acr/** and governance/reconciliations/** while allowing only additions, yet an ACR's own lifecycle (PROPOSED → ENDORSED → APPROVED → IMPLEMENTED) and a reconciliation's decision (STAGED → DECIDED) are modifications of existing records — and no ACR's authorized_paths covers its own record, so approving ACR-003 would require an approved ACR authorizing the edit of ACR-003.json, recursively. The principal mechanism ARCH-WF-002 delivers cannot complete its own lifecycle under its own protection model.
transitions.failure_reason: Circular ACR authorization: modifying an existing ACR/reconciliation record (any lifecycle advancement — including ACR-003's own approval, the REC-CAD-PARITY-011 decision, and every future ACR's lifecycle) is a protected-path violation that requires an approved ACR enumerating that record path; no ACR can authorize its own record, so the registry lifecycle deadlocks after creation. Required remediation: a finite, explicit bootstrap/lifecycle rule that permits narrowly authorized state transitions of ACR/reconciliation records without making the registries generally mutable — new proposals/staging stay allowed, lifecycle transitions become narrowly authorized, arbitrary existing-record edits stay blocked, protected implementation changes still require an approved ACR, and the normal VERIFIED gate is unchanged — covered by deterministic tests including a proof that ordinary modifications to existing ACR/reconciliation records remain blocked. No merge, no VERIFIED, no P012.

transitions.reason: CHANGES REQUESTED remediation complete and pushed to the open PR #101 (heads 5c7d55f the ruling record, 8eb7abb the registry lifecycle rule, 308c4de the docs). The circular ACR authorization is broken by the finite, explicit registry lifecycle rule: the two registry patterns (governance/acr/**, governance/reconciliations/**) are lifecycle-managed (a manifest change routed through ACR-003), and a modification of an EXISTING registry record is waived ONLY when it is a narrowly content-checked legal lifecycle transition — same identity, a legal status edge (single-gate or monotone composition), changed top-level fields EXACTLY {status} plus the edge's gate instruments, every instrument newly added with its authorizing role and required verdict (tools/governance/src/registry-lifecycle.ts). An ACR's own lifecycle advancement is now authorized by the lifecycle rules themselves — never by another ACR. New proposals/staging stay allowed; arbitrary existing-record edits (prose, authorized_paths, evidence, citations, instrument replacement, key removal, id changes, deletions) remain blocked — proven by deterministic tests including the authorized_paths-smuggling and git-level tamper cases; protected implementation changes still require an approved ACR; the normal VERIFIED gate is untouched.

Architect ruling on PR #101 (delivered through the session channel; GitHub cannot carry a formal REQUEST_CHANGES review because the repository owner authored the PR): CHANGES REQUESTED again — not approved for merge. The circular-authorization defect is substantially addressed and the lifecycle guard is much stronger, but another governance bypass was found: lifecycle bypass at record creation. The protected-path rule intentionally allows additions under governance/acr/** and governance/reconciliations/** (correct for creating proposals/staged reconciliations), but the validator does not require newly created REAL records to begin at their initial lifecycle states. A PR can therefore create governance/acr/ACR-004.json with status APPROVED (review and approval included) or even IMPLEMENTED; because the file did not exist on main, the protected-path check treats it as an allowed registry addition and the lifecycle-transition guard never sees a before/after pair, so there is no requirement that the record actually traversed PROPOSED → ENDORSED → APPROVED → IMPLEMENTED. The same bypass exists for reconciliations: a newly created real reconciliation can be introduced directly as DECIDED rather than STAGED → DECIDED. This is especially important because ACR-9xx/demo records are explicitly reserved for demonstration, meaning the validator needs a real-record bootstrap invariant rather than relying on the demo fixtures.
transitions.failure_reason: Creation-time lifecycle bypass: newly created non-demo registry records are not required to be born at their initial lifecycle states. Required correction — new ACR record → must be PROPOSED; new reconciliation → must be STAGED; then lifecycle-managed modifications may perform only the narrowly checked legal transitions. The fix must operate at the canonical validation/protected-path boundary, not merely in the PR template. Deterministic tests must prove: new real ACR with status APPROVED → BLOCKED; new real ACR with status IMPLEMENTED → BLOCKED; new real reconciliation DECIDED → BLOCKED; new real ACR with status PROPOSED → ALLOWED; new reconciliation with STAGED → ALLOWED; existing record legal lifecycle edge → ALLOWED; existing record arbitrary modification → BLOCKED. The prior circularity finding is resolved conceptually, but creation-time lifecycle bypass remains a governance integrity defect. No VERIFIED, no P012, and no merge until this is closed.

transitions.reason: Round-3 CHANGES REQUESTED remediation complete and pushed to the open PR #101 (heads 0905bf3 the ruling record, 9a8084d the creation invariant, 76353fa the CLI completion fix). The lifecycle bypass at record creation is closed at the canonical validation/protected-path boundary: a record newly created under governance/acr/** or governance/reconciliations/** must ACTUALLY traverse its lifecycle — the protected-path check reads the record's full commit history within the change (checkRegistryAdditionTraversal, tools/governance/src/registry-lifecycle.ts): the INTRODUCTION commit must be born at the INITIAL status (real ACR → PROPOSED, real reconciliation → STAGED) and EVERY later change to the same new record within the change must itself be a narrowly content-checked legal lifecycle transition. A record born mid-lifecycle (already APPROVED/IMPLEMENTED/DECIDED) is blocked with an explicit reason naming the introduction commit; an intra-change tamper (e.g. an authorized_paths expansion between legal-looking endpoints) is blocked because every step is checked; deletions mid-change are blocked; unreadable history fails closed. Demo fixtures (demo: true) are exempt from the initial-status rule but inert (they can never route protected-path changes or sanction real reconciliations; the ACR-9xx range and disclaimer are enforced by validate) — later edits to a new demo record within the same change are still checked as transitions. The traversal is also what keeps the documented review-time acts flow lawful: a record born PROPOSED on the PR branch advanced to APPROVED by the Architect's acts commit passes as REGISTRY ADITION + REGISTRY LIFECYCLE with the traversed edges named (dry-run verified). The general ACR-routing channel still authorizes explicitly enumerated out-of-band registrations. 39 new deterministic tests (199/199 total): the ruling's exact seven-row matrix (new real ACR APPROVED/IMPLEMENTED → BLOCKED; new real reconciliation DECIDED → BLOCKED; new real ACR PROPOSED → ALLOWED; new reconciliation STAGED → ALLOWED; existing record legal edge → ALLOWED; existing record arbitrary modification → BLOCKED) at unit, integration and git e2e level, the acts-flow and smuggle git e2e replays, and the traversal cases (multi-gate traversals, backwards steps, mid-change deletions, demo exemptions, fail-closed unreadable history).

A second real defect was found and fixed during submission: CI run 33333571893 failed the deterministic suite's 'CLI validate exits with the expected code' assertion — process.exit() truncated the tail of piped stdout (the exit code was intact; the Summary line was lost) — root-caused, reproduced locally (1/40 spawnSync runs against 9a8084d, stdout truncated at 29174/41358 bytes), fixed by completing commands via process.exitCode + natural exit (finish()) and proven lossless in 0/80 runs including under synthetic CPU load; CI green at 199/199 on 76353fa. evidence.description: A second real defect found and fixed during round-3 submission verification: governance CI run 33333571893 on head 9a8084d failed the deterministic suite's 'CLI validate exits with the expected code on the real repository' assertion — the CLI's exit code was intact (1, as expected) but stdout ended without the 'Summary:' line. Root cause: the CLI completed every command with process.exit(code) immediately after printing; process.exit does not wait for pending libuv stdio writes, so on a loaded runner the final queued pipe writes are dropped (the failure is timing-sensitive: all earlier CI runs passed with the same latent defect). Reproduced locally: 40 spawnSync runs of the exact test's invocation against 9a8084d (Node 22) lost the stdout tail once — truncated at 29174 of 41358 bytes with status intact, matching the CI failure shape exactly. Fix (commit 76353fa): every command path (validate, check-protected, check-verified-revisions) completes via finish() — process.exitCode + natural exit, letting stdio drain (usage() keeps its hard exit: three short stderr lines). Proof: 80 further spawnSync runs against the fixed code (40 normal + 40 under synthetic CPU load), 0 tails lost; all command exit codes preserved (validate 1 designed, check-verified-revisions 0, check-protected 1 pre-acts); CI run 33334077503 on 76353fa then passed the full deterministic suite 199/199.
